prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In her field guide, one botanist describes these crusts as a living ______.

worlds.passage: Farmers in one northern valley once built hundreds of dry stone walls, and today the walls are coated with lichens, slow-growing crusts of fungus and algae. The crusts spread onto the walls from nearby cliffs after the walls were built, and they grow at no steady rate, but one species withers within weeks whenever sulfur in the air rises, long before crops or people show harm, and the stone beneath it stays bare of soil. In her field guide, one botanist describes these crusts as a living ______.
worlds.explanation: One species withers whenever sulfur in the air rises, well before crops or people are harmed, so the crusts give early warning: they are a living "sentinel." "Timeline" fails because they grow at no steady rate, so their size dates nothing; "vestige" fails because they arrived only after the walls were built; "scaffold" fails because the stone beneath stays bare of soil, so nothing builds on them.

timeline.why: Without a steady growth rate, the crusts cannot record how much time has passed.

vestige.quote: spread onto the walls from nearby cliffs after the walls were built
vestige.why: Recent arrivals are not the surviving remnant of something older.

scaffold.quote: stone beneath it stays bare of soil
scaffold.why: No soil forms, so the crusts support no later growth.
